title: HelperSessionOutputRows
description: One batch of the rows that left a session's screen, streamed from the helper the moment they left it (nocx-2v80t.3.6). The owner's decision gives the helper no copy of departed rows — ghostty's own scrollback is the buffer — so this document is the only place the rows go. The rows ride in the frame contract's row vocabulary (nocx-zg3k3.2.12: a row as its text in column order, a sparse list of the positions whose codepoint count or column footprint departs from the default, and style runs measured in columns), encoded by the runtime's own row encoder, so what a coordinator stores from the stream and what it paints live are one shape. Every row is carried exactly once, in stream order; a batch names the absolute index its first row holds, counting every row the session has ever seen depart, so the order is checkable rather than trusted.

fromRow.description: The absolute index of this batch's first row: the count of rows the session had seen depart before it, whether or not any consumer was bound when they did. Indices are the session's, never the consumer's, so a consumer that attaches late continues where the session left off and a confirmed-written mark names a position both ends can check.

lostRows.description: Two sources add into one count, and both keep this batch's FromRow minus the row count after the delivery before it exact — never a gap the coordinator has to invent a reason for (a discontinuous FromRow whose lostRows does not measure the gap precisely is refused, content.AppendBlockRows). The first is the FEEDS the emulator struck immediately before this batch's first row: the ABI carries no departure counter, and a prune inside a feed mixes with that feed's own departures in one depth reading, so the rows a prune took are unknowable by contract — one struck feed reads as one, a deliberately symbolic count rather than a manufactured row estimate. The second is an exact row count: rows the session's own bridge had to drop before they ever reached a batch, because the wire had fallen a whole queue behind (nocx-2v80t.3.15) — the runtime's own row index still advanced past them, so this is what tells the coordinator precisely how many, never a silent hole. An ordinary batch, with a keeping-up wire and no struck feed, carries none.

rows.description: The rows that left, oldest first, in the frame contract's row shape. The array is carried whole: a batch with no rows and a loss marker is how a hole at the very end of an interval is stated, so an empty array is an answer and not an absence.
